text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia and Greece to announce decision that Macedonian citizens born in Aegean (Greek) Macedonia can travel to this country only if their passports list Greece as their country of birth.
- Macedonian foreign ministry asked the Bosnian government to say if it will introduce visas for Macedonian citizens.

- During his visit to New York, Macedonian Foreign Minsiter Ljubomir Frckovski won support from several Asian and African countries for Macedonia's candidacy as a non-permanent member of the U.N. Security Council.
- OSCE mission in Macedonia will monitor local elections on Novemvber 17, said head of mission Christian Faber Roth.

- Macedonian and Yugoslav transport ministers Dimitar Buzlevski and Zoran Vujovic announced in Belgrade Tuesday that all customs duties at the Macedonia-Yugoslav border are to be abolished from October 7.

- One hundred and fourty children from the village of Bogovinje near Tetovo have contracted food poisoning symptoms. Skopje clinics are analysing their blood to determine the exact nature of the poisoning.
